title: Week of Aug 24–30 · Foundations: 4 Lifts, 2 Runs
subtitle: New structure this week: four strength nights built around hip flexor and core strength, two short easy runs. Light weights on purpose — this week is about the movements, not the numbers.
goals: Make all four lifts. Weights stay light (RPE 6, ~3 reps in the tank) — after a year away, week 1 is practice, not a test
Hip flexor and core work is the main event, not the add-on. Do those sets as carefully as the squats
Both runs short and easy (RPE 3–4, walk breaks fine). Note how the knee feels during and after each one — that note from your 4-miler is steering this plan
Log every session, even one line. Weights you log this week become next week's starting points
Still on the list: connect Strava at workoutplanning-production.up.railway.app/api/strava/connect/emma so runs and heart rate show up automatically
review: Your new week, built the way you asked: four lifting days with the focus on hip flexor strength and core, plus two runs. Since it's been about a year since you lifted regularly, everything starts back at basics — Back Squat at your 65 lb, light dumbbells everywhere else, and form cues on every card. The plan of attack: each lift day has 2–3 basic strength moves, then a hips block, then a core block. That hips-and-core emphasis is also exactly what your knee wants — you logged 'my knee hurts' after the 4-miler, and stronger hips (especially the outside-hip and hip flexor muscles) plus patient run volume is the standard fix. So runs this week are 2 miles or less, genuinely easy, with a 🚴 bike swap on every run card if the knee complains at all. Expect some soreness after Monday and Tuesday — that's normal after a layoff. If it piles up, drop the last set of each exercise and carry on. Log it all, and next week builds from what you actually did.

days.name: Foundation A · Squat + Hip Flexors
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)

items.note: Start back at your 65 lb, RPE 6 — about 3 reps in the tank. After a year away the goal is 24 smooth reps, not a heavy bar. If it moves well all week, small bump next week.
items.focus: Brace, chest tall, knees track over toes, squat to a depth you control.

items.note: Pick a weight that's RPE 6–7. Push-ups from the floor or an incline are a full substitute.
items.focus: Shoulder blades set, lower under control, press up and slightly together.

items.note: Light and strict beats heavy and swingy.
items.focus: Flat back, pull to your hip, squeeze the shoulder blade.

items.note: The hips block. Psoas march: on your back, band around both feet, drive one knee toward your chest against the band, slow and controlled — this is the actual hip flexor strength work. Straight into side-lying leg lifts, then 45s rest, 3 rounds. No band? March slowly in place driving each knee above hip height with a 1s hold.
items.focus: Low back stays glued to the floor on the march; toes forward and hip stacked on the leg lifts.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: dead bug → plank, three rounds, ~20s between moves.
items.focus: Ribs down, low back pressed into the floor, opposite arm and leg reach long.
Straight line head to heels, glutes tight, breathe — don't hold your breath.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Foundation B · Hinge + Glutes
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)
Banded lateral walks (or side steps) — 10 each way

items.note: Light dumbbells, RPE 6. This is a hinge, not a squat — the whole point today is grooving the hip-back pattern.
items.focus: Soft knees, hips back, feel the hamstrings, flat back the whole way.

items.note: One light-to-medium dumbbell held at your chest. A second squat pattern in the week, deliberately lighter than Monday's.
items.focus: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom, tall chest, drive up through the whole foot.

items.note: Seated or standing, light DBs, RPE 6–7.
items.focus: Ribs down, press straight up, finish with biceps by your ears.

items.note: The hips block: 10 single-leg bridges per side straight into 12 clamshells per side, 45s rest, 3 rounds. Band optional on the clamshells. This pair is your knee insurance.
items.focus: Bridges: drive through the heel, hips level. Clamshells: slow, toes together, don't let the hip roll back.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: side plank → bird dog, three rounds. From the knees is a fine starting version.
items.focus: Hips stacked and lifted, straight line shoulder to feet.
Slow reach, hips square to the floor, pause 2s at full stretch.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Easy Run · 2 mi (or Bike)
warmup: Ankle circles + a few walking lunges

run.title: Easy conversational run — knee is the headline
run.detail: Two easy miles at a pace where you could chat the whole way; walk breaks are completely fine and don't make it not-count. You logged 'my knee hurts' after the 4-miler, so this run is also a test read: note whether the knee says anything during or after. A little awareness that fades is okay; actual pain, or anything that changes your stride — stop, tap the 🚴 toggle next time, and ride easy instead. Legs may feel heavy from Mon/Tue lifting; that's expected, go slower.

hr.zone: Easy / conversational (RPE 3–4) — connect Strava and future runs get HR zones
hr.main: RPE 3–4 — full sentences the whole way
hr.note: The lifting is what's pushing this week. Runs are practice moving, nothing more.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Foundation C · Squat 2 + Hip Flexors
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)

items.note: Second exposure. Same 65 lb unless Monday felt easy (RPE ≤6 on every set) — then 70 is earned.
items.focus: Same cues as Monday: brace, chest tall, controlled depth. Aim for these to look identical to Monday's.

items.note: RPE 6–7. If the gym's busy, one-arm rows cover it.
items.focus: Chest up, pull the bar to your collarbone, elbows down and back — no leaning way back.

items.note: Bodyweight first — add light DBs only if it feels solid and the knee is quiet. Reverse (stepping back) is the knee-friendly version, which is why it's this and not forward lunges.
items.focus: Long stride back, tall torso, drive through the front heel to stand.

items.n: Hip Flexor Raise + Leg Raise superset
items.note: The hips block, rotated from Monday. Standing raise: drive one knee above hip height and hold 2s at the top (hold a wall for balance; add a light ankle weight or band when 8 gets easy). Then lie down for 10 slow straight-leg raises. 45s rest, 3 rounds.
items.focus: Stand tall — no leaning back to cheat the knee up. On leg raises, low back stays pressed to the floor.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: hollow hold → shoulder taps, three rounds. Bend the knees to shorten the lever if your low back arches.
items.focus: Low back pressed down, ribs pulled in, arms and legs only as long as you can control.
Feet a bit wider, hips dead still — the tap is the easy part, the not-rocking is the exercise.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Rest Day
days.desc: Full rest, and you've earned it — three lifts and a run in four days. If you want to move, a gentle walk or easy stretch (hips and hip flexors especially) is plenty. A Sculpt class fits here too if you're feeling good — just log it. Otherwise, nothing to do but eat and sleep.
fields: What did you do? (fine if nothing)
How sore are you, 1–10, and where?

days.name: Foundation D · Press + Glutes
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)
Arm circles + band pull-aparts (or wall slides) — 10 each
Banded lateral walks (or side steps) — 10 each way

items.note: Second exposure this week. Same weight as Monday unless it was easy — then one DB size up.
items.focus: Shoulder blades set, controlled lowering, press up and slightly together.

items.note: Second hinge of the week. Same weight as Tuesday, aim for smoother reps.
items.focus: Soft knees, hips back, hamstrings load, flat back.

items.note: A dumbbell across your hips (a folded towel makes it comfortable). Pause 1s at the top of every rep.
items.focus: Drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to lift, ribs down at the top — no low-back arch.

items.note: The hips block: 10 banded side-steps each way straight into the psoas march from Monday, 45s rest, 3 rounds. Third hip flexor touch of the week — this is the muscle you asked to build, so it gets frequency.
items.focus: Stay low in a quarter-squat on the walks; slow controlled knee drives on the march.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: plank → side plank, three rounds. Add ~5–10s to Monday's plank time if it was solid.
items.focus: Straight line head to heels, glutes tight, breathe.
Hips stacked and lifted the whole time; from the knees is fine.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Short Easy Run · 1.5–2 mi (or Bike / Walk)
warmup: Ankle circles + a few walking lunges

run.title: Easy shakeout to close the week
run.detail: Run number two: 1.5–2 miles, genuinely easy, daylight instead of evening if you like. Same knee rule as Wednesday — note how it behaves during and after, and if it complains, the 🚴 bike or even a long walk closes the week just as well. Then look back: four lifts and two runs on the new plan. Whatever got logged, next week starts from there.

hr.main: RPE 3–4 — you should be able to talk in full sentences
hr.cool: 5 min walk, then stretch while warm
hr.note: After a 4-lift week your legs will be tired. Slower than feels necessary is exactly right.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 60s each side
